title: When NOT to make a sub-plan
idea: MEET: naming a job is great for reuse, but not every line needs its own name. No code.

exercises.prompt: Which job is clearly worth naming as a sub-plan?
options: A border printed at the top and bottom of every page
A single print used exactly once
exercises.explanation: A job used in many places earns a name. One-off single actions usually don't need one.

exercises.prompt: Every single line of a plan should be turned into its own named sub-plan.
exercises.explanation: No. Over-naming tiny one-off lines adds clutter. Name jobs that repeat or that group meaningful work.

exercises.prompt: Which jobs are GOOD candidates to name? (Pick all.)
options: a greeting shown for every player
totalling the basket, reused per customer
exercises.explanation: Repeated or reused jobs earn names. A one-time single print does not need its own name.

exercises.prompt: What's the downside of naming a trivial one-off line?
options: Extra clutter for no reuse benefit
exercises.explanation: Naming shines with reuse. A one-off gains nothing and just adds an extra name to read.

exercises.prompt: Match each job to 'name it' or 'leave inline'.
exercises.explanation: Name reusable or meaningful jobs; leave trivial one-offs inline. Judgment, like deciding whether to split.

exercises.prompt: A job that groups several meaningful steps can be worth naming even if used once, for clarity.
exercises.explanation: True. Naming can also make a plan readable by labelling a chunk of work - clarity, not just reuse.

exercises.prompt: The two main reasons to name a job are...
options: to make it slower, and longer
to hide it, and confuse readers
exercises.explanation: You name a job to reuse it or to label a meaningful chunk clearly. Both are good reasons.

exercises.prompt: REVIEW: deciding WHETHER to name a job is like which earlier decision?
options: deciding whether a task is worth splitting
exercises.explanation: Same judgment as 'should I split this?' from Unit 69. You weigh reuse and clarity against clutter.

exercises.prompt: Good naming is about judgment, not a rule to name absolutely everything.
exercises.explanation: Yes. Name what helps (reuse, clarity); skip what doesn't. Thoughtful naming keeps plans clean.

options: name jobs that repeat or clarify; leave trivial one-offs inline
exercises.explanation: Name for reuse and clarity. Not every line needs a name - judgment keeps the plan tidy.
